sections.content:
Population change in Aylesbury Vale

The population in Aylesbury Vale is projected to increase from 199,448 in 2018 to 223,248 people in 2028.

The biggest factor in population change is net internal migration, which will increase the population by 9,644.

This will also be the biggest factor in population change in most areas in England.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Aylesbury Vale
sections.subtitle: How the population is projected to change, by cause
sections.source: Office for National Statistics – Subnational population projections for England.

sections.content:
In Aylesbury Vale, this is how all the different factors are projected to contribute to population change between 2018 and 2028:

  • More births than deaths mean that the population is projected to increase by 3.3% (6,579), compared with an increase of 1.6% in England, with 23,211 births and 16,632 deaths in Aylesbury Vale between 2018 and 2028.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other areas in England) is projected to increase the population by 4.8% (9,644), with 115,433 people entering the area and 105,789 people leaving the area between 2018 and 2028.
  • Net cross-border migration (between UK nations) is projected to reduce the population by 0.5% (928), with 2,572 people entering the area and 3,500 people leaving the area between 2018 and 2028.
  • Net international migration is projected to increase the population by 4.2% (8,448), compared with an increase of 3.5% in England, with 15,716 people entering the area and 7,268 people leaving the area between 2018 and 2028.

sections.content:
Age profile in Aylesbury Vale in 2028

The median age in Aylesbury Vale is projected to rise from 39 years in 2018 to 41 years in 2028.

In England, the median age is projected to be 40 years in 2028.

Between 2018 and 2028, the proportion of people aged 65 years or over in Aylesbury Vale is projected to rise from 17% to 19%.

sections.title: The 60 to 69 age group are set to see the largest increases in Aylesbury Vale over the next 10 years.
sections.subtitle: Proportion of population by 10 year age bands, 2018 and 2028
sections.source: Office for National Statistics – Subnational population projections for England.

sections.content:
Between 2018 and 2028, the working population (people aged 16 years to State Pension age) in Aylesbury Vale is projected to stay the same, at around 60%.

The old age dependency ratio (the number of people of pensionable age for every 1,000 people of working age) is projected to rise from 273 to 318 over the same time period.

This is below average for England in 2028 (319 per 1,000). Nationally, a high old age dependency ratio means more older people are financially reliant on the working population to pay for pensions.

How will the number of young people change in Aylesbury Vale?

Between 2018 and 2028, the number of people aged 18 years and under in Aylesbury Vale is projected to stay the same, at around 24%.

This is slightly above average for England in 2028 (23%).
